lessons.title: Mean, median, mode and range for tables
lessons.programRef: O Level Mathematics — Statistics (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Find the mean, median, mode and range from a frequency table.
Estimate the mean of grouped data using mid-class values.
reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: The mean from a table
blocks.md: For a frequency table with values x and frequencies f (and grouped data using the **mid-class value** for x):

blocks.title: Median, mode, range
blocks.md:
- **Mode**: the value with the greatest frequency (modal class for grouped data).
- **Median**: the middle value when ordered: position $\frac{n+1}{2}$; use the cumulative frequency to find it.
- **Range** = largest value − smallest value.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Dividing Σfx by the **number of rows** instead of Σf.
- Reading the highest frequency as the mode: the mode is the **value** with that frequency.
- Using class boundaries instead of mid-class values for the grouped mean.

blocks.title: Example 1: frequency table
blocks.statement: The marks of 24 students out of 6 are: 2 (3 students), 3 (5), 4 (8), 5 (6), 6 (2). Find the mean, median and mode.
steps: Cumulative frequencies: 3, 8, 16, 22, 24. The 12th and 13th values are both 4: median 4.
The highest frequency, 8, is at the mark 4: mode 4.

blocks.title: Example 2: grouped data
blocks.statement: Heights (cm) of 40 students: 140–149 (4), 150–159 (10), 160–169 (14), 170–179 (8), 180–189 (4). Estimate the mean and state the modal class.
steps: The largest frequency is 14: modal class 160–169.

lessons.title: Cumulative frequency, median and quartiles
lessons.programRef: O Level Mathematics — Statistics (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Build a cumulative frequency table and draw the curve (ogive).
Estimate the median, quartiles and interquartile range from the curve.
Read the number of values above or below a given value.
reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.md:
1. Add the frequencies to get the **cumulative frequency** (running total) and plot it against the **upper class boundary**.
2. Join the points with a smooth curve (or straight segments), starting at the lowest boundary with cumulative frequency 0.
3. For n values, read the **median** at n/2, the **lower quartile** Q1 at n/4 and the **upper quartile** Q3 at 3n/4.

blocks.title: Spread
blocks.md: The interquartile range measures the spread of the middle half of the data:

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Plotting against the class midpoint or the lower boundary: use the **upper** boundary.
- Reading the median at (n + 1)/2 on a grouped curve: use n/2.
- Reading the wrong axis: horizontal for the data value, vertical for the cumulative frequency.

blocks.title: Example 1: medians and quartiles
blocks.statement: The marks of 50 students (upper boundaries 20, 40, 60, 80, 100) have frequencies 5, 12, 18, 10, 5. Find the cumulative frequencies and estimate the median.
steps: The median is at 50 ÷ 2 = 25th value, in the class 40–60 (cumulative 17 to 35).
By interpolation: 40 + (25 − 17) ÷ 18 × 20 ≈ 48.9. Reading from the curve gives about 49.

blocks.title: Example 2: quartiles and a count
blocks.statement: Using the same data, estimate Q1, Q3, the interquartile range and the number of students who scored more than 70.
steps: At 70 the cumulative frequency is 35 + 10 × (70 − 60) ÷ 20 = 40, so 50 − 40 = 10 students scored more than 70.

lessons.title: Histograms with unequal class widths
lessons.programRef: O Level Mathematics — Statistics (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Draw and read a histogram with unequal classes.
Find frequencies from the areas of the bars.
reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Frequency density
blocks.md: In a histogram the **area** of each bar (not its height) is proportional to the frequency. So the height is the frequency density:

blocks.title: Reading a histogram
blocks.md: Frequency of a class = frequency density × class width (the area of the bar). Bars touch each other (continuous data) and there are no gaps. The vertical axis is labelled 'frequency density'.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Drawing the frequency as the height when class widths are unequal.
- Leaving gaps between bars of continuous data.
- Mixing up class width and class boundaries: width = upper − lower.

blocks.title: Example 1: frequency density
blocks.statement: The ages of 72 people are: 10–20 (12), 20–30 (18), 30–50 (24), 50–80 (18). Find the frequency density of each class.
steps: These are the heights of the bars.

blocks.title: Example 2: from the histogram
blocks.statement: In a histogram the bar for 30–50 has height 1.2 (frequency density). How many people are in that class, and what fraction of the 72 people is that?
